pure-announcement.rationale: This is NVIDIA's own launch post for the Ising model family ('launches with two breakthrough models'), built around its benchmark wins, parameter counts, and get-started links; the pre-decoder idea appears only as this product's feature, not as a technique covered independently of the launch.

duplicate.rationale: None of the nearest concepts (W2S generalization, acceptability envelopes, SLO burn rate, Code Mode MCP, RAG) touch quantum calibration or error-correction decoding.

unfalsifiable.rationale: Claims are tied to checkable artifacts — the QCalEval dataset on HuggingFace, research papers, and open model weights — so a reader can verify them.

durability.rationale: The load-bearing content is launch-cycle specifics — Ising-Calibration-1's 3.27%/9.68%/14.5% margins over named rival model versions, 912K/1.79M parameter counts, and per-GPU microsecond figures — exactly the benchmark-delta material that stales within a product cycle.

actionability.rationale: Every concrete step is a pointer into NVIDIA's own stack (NIM, cuStabilizer, NeMo Agent Toolkit, HuggingFace checkpoints); a reader outside that product line gets no build-or-decide guidance.

atomicity.rationale: It bundles two separable model domains — an agentic calibration VLM and CNN pre-decoders for surface-code QEC — plus a benchmark release, held together only by the shared launch.
